definition: A quantity that has magnitude (size) only, with no direction. Examples: speed, distance, mass, temperature, energy.
A quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Examples: velocity, displacement, force, acceleration, momentum.
The distance travelled in a specific direction. A vector quantity measured in metres (m).
The speed of an object in a given direction. A vector quantity measured in m/s.
A force that acts between objects that are physically touching, such as friction, tension, normal contact force or air resistance.
A force that acts between objects that are not touching, such as gravity, electrostatic force or magnetic force.
The force of gravity acting on an object. W = mg. Measured in newtons (N). Depends on gravitational field strength.
The amount of matter in an object. Measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
The force of gravity per unit mass at a point in a gravitational field. On Earth g ≈ 10 N/kg.
The single force that has the same effect as all the forces acting on an object combined. Found by adding forces as vectors.
When the resultant force on an object is zero — the object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
The energy transferred when a force moves an object through a distance. W = Fs. Measured in joules (J).
When an object returns to its original shape and size after the force is removed.
When an object does not return to its original shape and size after the force is removed — permanently deformed.
The extension of a spring is directly proportional to the force applied, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded. F = ke.
A measure of the stiffness of a spring. The force needed to extend or compress it by 1 metre. Measured in N/m. Symbol: k.
The maximum force beyond which a spring will not return to its original length — permanent deformation occurs.
A graph showing how the distance travelled by an object changes over time. The gradient gives the speed.
A graph showing how the velocity of an object changes over time. Gradient gives acceleration; area under graph gives distance.
The rate of change of velocity. a = (v - u) / t or F = ma. Measured in m/s². Can be positive (speeding up) or negative (decelerating).
An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a resultant force. Objects resist changes in motion.
The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the resultant force and inversely proportional to its mass. F = ma.
For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always act in pairs on different objects.
The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. Related to its mass.
The distance a vehicle travels during the driver's reaction time before braking begins.
The distance a vehicle travels after braking until it stops. Depends on speed, braking force, road conditions and tyre condition.
The total distance needed to stop a vehicle. Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance.
The product of an object's mass and velocity. p = mv. Measured in kg m/s. A vector quantity.
The total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after, provided no external forces act.
The change in momentum of an object. Impulse = force × time = Δp. Measured in N s or kg m/s.
